Definition: from G5522; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene:--earthy.
BiblicalUsage: Choikos is earthy, made of dust, and Paul uses it to set the first man against the last. The first man is of the earth, earthy, and as is the earthy so are they that are earthy, but we shall also bear the image of the heavenly, because the last Adam is a quickening spirit.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's earthy man is me by nature, dust that returns to dust, and the heavenly man is me by grace. I hold that the change from earthy to heavenly is the whole hope of the resurrection.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
